chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Sulaym, the freedman of Tirbal, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who had intercourse with his slave-girl, and he used to send her on his errands, and she became pregnant, and news reached him that she had been unchaste; he (Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him) said: 'If she gives birth, he keeps the child and does not sell him, and he makes for him a share from his house.'

He said: Then it was said: A man who had intercourse with his slave-girl, and he had not sent her on his errands, and he accused her (of unchastity) and she became pregnant; he said: 'When she gives birth, he keeps the child and does not sell him, and he makes for him a share from his house and his wealth, and this case is not like that one.'
ai.seo_question: What are the inheritance rights of a slave's child when the master accuses her of unchastity?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the status of *ibn al-mil'ah* (child of the slave-girl) by distinguishing between a master who utilized her for household duties, implying greater fidelity, and one who did not, affecting the presumption of paternity. In both scenarios, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) mandates that the child be retained and granted a share of the master's estate, ensuring their financial security despite the ambiguity of lineage. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic emphasis on preserving the child's rights and preventing their sale, reflecting a compassionate approach to mixed-status families.
